nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$ let $f_k(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every set of $m$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ in general position (any at most $k + 1$ of them affinely independent) contains $n$ points in convex position (none of them in the convex hull of the others), with $f_k(n) = 0$ if there is no such $m$. It is not the case that for every $k \ge 2$ there is a real $c > 0$ with $(1 + c)^n < f_k(n)$ for all…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 651 has a negative answer

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$ let $f_k(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every set of $m$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ in general position (any at most $k + 1$ of them affinely independent) contains $n$ points in convex position (none of them in the convex hull of the others), with $f_k(n) = 0$ if there is no such $m$. The claim is that for every $k \ge 2$ there is a real $c > 0$ with $(1 + c)^n < f_k(n)$ for all…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 651: exponential growth of convex position thresholds

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, $f_k(n)$ is the least natural number $m$ such that every set of $m$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ in general position (any at most $k + 1$ of them affinely independent) contains $n$ points in convex position (none of them in the convex hull of the others). If there is no such $m$, then $f_k(n) = 0$.
nodes.title: Convex position threshold

nodes.summary: A set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ contains a convex $n$-gon if there is a set $S \subseteq P$ of exactly $n$ points that is convex independent: no point of $S$ lies in the convex hull of the other points of $S$.
nodes.title: Sets containing a convex $n$-gon

nodes.summary: A set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, finite or infinite, is in _general position_ if no three distinct points of $X$ are collinear and no four distinct points of $X$ lie on a common circle.
nodes.title: Points in general position

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be an oriented two-dimensional Euclidean affine space. Points $p_0, \dots, p_{n-1} \in P$ form a counterclockwise convex polygon if for all indices $i < j < k$ the oriented angle $\measuredangle p_i p_j p_k$ at $p_j$ has sign $-1$, that is, $p_i, p_j, p_k$ are not collinear and lie in counterclockwise order with respect to the orientation of $P$. Every list of at most two points qualifies.
nodes.title: Counterclockwise convex polygons

nodes.summary: If three points $A, B, C$ of an oriented two-dimensional Euclidean affine space are affinely independent, then $A, B, C$ form a convex polygon.
nodes.title: Affinely independent triples are convex polygons

nodes.summary: Points $p_0, \dots, p_{n-1}$ of an oriented two-dimensional Euclidean affine space form a convex polygon if one of the lists $p_0, p_1, \dots, p_{n-1}$ and $p_0, p_{n-1}, p_{n-2}, \dots, p_1$ is a counterclockwise convex polygon: for any three of its entries $q, r, s$, in the order in which they occur in that list, the oriented angle $\measuredangle q r s$ at $r$ has sign $-1$. Thus for $n \ge 3$ the points are the…
nodes.title: Convex polygons

nodes.summary: If a family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of an affine space over a division ring $k$ is affinely independent over $k$, then it is in general position through dimension $d$ for every $d \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Affinely independent families are in general position

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a division ring and $V$ a vector space over $k$, with projective space $\mathbb{P}(V)$. A family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of $\mathbb{P}(V)$ is in general position through dimension $d \in \mathbb{N}$ if for every finite set $S \subseteq \iota$ of at most $d + 1$ indices, the subfamily $(p_i)_{i \in S}$ is projectively independent.
nodes.title: General position of projective points

nodes.summary: If a family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(V)$ of a vector space $V$ over a division ring $k$ is projectively independent, then it is in general position through dimension $d$ for every $d \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Projectively independent families are in general position

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a division ring and $P$ an affine space over $k$. A family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of $P$ is in general position through dimension $d \in \mathbb{N}$ if for every finite set $S \subseteq \iota$ of at most $d + 1$ indices, the subfamily $(p_i)_{i \in S}$ is affinely independent over $k$.
nodes.title: General position of affine points

nodes.summary: A set $A$ in a space with a distance function $d$ is isosceles-free if there are no three distinct points $x, y, z \in A$ such that two of the distances $d(x, y)$, $d(y, z)$, $d(z, x)$ are equal.
nodes.title: Isosceles-free sets

nodes.summary: Points $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}^2$ are the vertices, in counterclockwise order, of an isosceles trapezoid if they are in strictly convex position and listed counterclockwise (for any three of them $p, q, r$, in the order in which they occur in the list $a, b, c, d$, the oriented angle $\measuredangle p q r$ at $q$ has sign $-1$), the line through $a$ and $b$ is parallel to the line through $c$ and $d$ (the two…
nodes.title: Isosceles trapezoids

nodes.summary: Points $a, b, c$ of a Euclidean affine space are the vertices of a right-angled triangle if they are pairwise distinct and the unoriented angle at one of the three vertices equals $\pi / 2$: $\angle bac = \pi / 2$, $\angle abc = \pi / 2$ or $\angle bca = \pi / 2$.
nodes.title: Right-angled triangles

nodes.summary: For a finite set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and a point $x \in X$, let $R_X(x)$ be the number of distinct distances $\lvert y - x \rvert$ from $x$ to the points $y \in X$ other than $x$. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $g(n)$ is the maximum, over all sets $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of exactly $n$ points, of the number of distinct values among the numbers $R_X(x)$ with $x \in X$.
nodes.title: Maximum number of distinct distance counts

nodes.summary: Let $d \le e$ be natural numbers. If a family of points of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(V)$ of a vector space $V$ over a division ring $k$ is in general position through dimension $e$, then it is in general position through dimension $d$.
nodes.title: General position in projective space is monotone in the dimension

nodes.summary: Let $d \le e$ be natural numbers. If a family of points of an affine space over a division ring $k$ is in general position through dimension $e$, then it is in general position through dimension $d$.
nodes.title: General position in affine space is monotone in the dimension

nodes.summary: A set $S$ of points in a Euclidean affine space has no $n$ collinear points if no subset of $S$ consisting of exactly $n$ points is collinear.
nodes.title: Sets with no $n$ collinear points

nodes.summary: A set $A$ of points in the plane is non-trilinear if no three distinct points of $A$ lie on a common line.
nodes.title: Sets with no three collinear points

nodes.summary: Let $\omega$ be the area form of the given orientation of the Euclidean plane, so that $\omega(u, v)$ is the signed area of the parallelogram spanned by the vectors $u$ and $v$. For points $a$, $b$, $c$ of the plane, the oriented area of the triangle with vertices $a$, $b$, $c$ is the real number $\omega(a - c, b - c) / 2$.
nodes.title: Oriented triangle area

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a ternary relation on a type $\alpha$ and let $s \subseteq \alpha$. The relation $r$ holds triplewise on $s$ if $r(x, y, z)$ holds for all pairwise distinct $x, y, z \in s$.
nodes.title: Relation holding triplewise on a set

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
